summary: Samoa is one of the most open countries in the world: visitors of every nationality are issued a free 90-day entry permit on arrival, with no visa and no online authorization to arrange, provided you hold onward travel and somewhere to stay.

primarySources.name: Samoa Immigration — Ministry of the Prime Minister and Cabinet

defaultSource.name: Samoa Immigration (Ministry of the Prime Minister and Cabinet) — Border Services

conflict.name: UK FCDO — Samoa travel advice: entry requirements
conflict.states: You can visit Samoa without a visa for up to 60 days

safety.text: Samoa is calm and welcoming, with low levels of violent crime. The usual issues are petty theft from open fales and vehicles, strong ocean currents and reef cuts, and driving hazards — narrow roads, roaming dogs and pigs, and driving on the left since 2009.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says the sale of alcohol is prohibited on Sundays. The UK's says drinking alcohol in public is illegal except at bars or restaurants, and that the legal drinking age is 21.

The UK government's travel advice says local communities expect modest dress in towns and villages; swimwear is fine on the beach or by streams and waterfalls but likely to draw negative attention elsewhere. Canada's advises asking permission before entering a lagoon, as villages may hold customary rights over it, and before photographing people.

Traffic drives on the left (Canada's travel advice). The UK government says you must buy a temporary driving permit, using your home licence, which car rental companies will help with and which covers up to 90 days a year; speed limits are 40 km/h in towns and villages and 56 km/h elsewhere, and any accident must be reported to the police within 24 hours.
Canada's travel advice says ATMs are mostly in and around Apia, with one on Savai'i and none elsewhere, so carry enough tālā before leaving Apia.
The UK government's travel advice says the tropical cyclone season normally runs from November to the end of April, and that heavier rainfall inland can cause flooding.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Samoa?
faq.answer: No. Samoa gives citizens of every country a free visitor entry permit on arrival, valid for up to 90 days. There is nothing to apply for in advance — just arrive with a passport valid six months, a confirmed onward ticket and details of where you are staying.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Samoa?
faq.answer: The entry permit is issued for up to 90 days. If you want to stay longer, the Immigration Division in Apia can extend it: apply before the permit expires, with an onward ticket and evidence of funds. No current fee is published online, so ask the office.

faq.question: Do I need a return ticket to enter Samoa?
faq.answer: Yes. The free permit is conditional on holding a confirmed onward or return ticket, and airlines check it at check-in. You should also be able to name accommodation for at least the first part of your stay.

faq.question: What vaccinations do I need for Samoa?
faq.answer: Only a yellow fever certificate, and only if you arrive from or have transited a yellow fever risk country. Samoa's Ministry of Health has no health-related travel restrictions in place, and after the 2019 measles epidemic being up to date with MMR vaccination is sensible. The UK government's travel advice lists dengue and Zika among the health risks, so take precautions against mosquito bites.
